text:
alex: Heads up — sudden GPU capacity drop in us-east1-prod, ~18% units gone offline, service error rates up. seeing Xid errors + network timeouts from the same racks. anyone watching?
ops-bot: [alert] us-east1-gpu-pool: capacity_drop=18% cpu_alerts=0 xid_rate=62/min net_err=404/sec
maya: :eyes: I'm pulling telemetry now, can you post a couple of example logs (nvidia-smi / dmesg) from affected hosts?
ravi: grabbed one host (gpu-rack12-node07):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (23): 13ffff00
[ 1234.568000] pcieport 0000:05:00.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: ID 00
[ 1234.568100] mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: mlx5: hw timeout (sleeping)
```
lina: that's noisy. ECC counters spike too? maya, can you dump `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` for that node?
maya: ECC summary attached (snippet):
```
GPU 0 ECC errors: L1=0 L2=0 DRAM=12
GPU 1 ECC errors: L1=0 L2=0 DRAM=15
```
ben: network timeouts coincide with a flurry of retransmits on the top-of-rack switch. infra said a microcode push rolled out last night to 3 racks in us-east1. could be related.
alex: ops: any rolling changes to NIC firmware or SR-IOV configs?
sre-oncall: Confirmed — we pushed NIC microcode 2026-02-18 03:40 UTC to racks 10-14. Rolling back right now for racks >10. Initiating partial rollback and drain of the most affected nodes.
maya: starting targeted drains on node07/08/09 in rack12. using `kubectl drain gpu-rack12-node07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
ravi: also seeing PCIe AER corrected errors before GPU Xid spikes — suggests link flakiness first, then GPU faults. recommend reducing load and evicting pods to test.
lina: agree. let's avoid mass drains until rollback confirmed. do canaries: drain one node, wait 5m, monitor Xid.
alex: good plan. can we fall back to secondary region for heavy workloads? what is cost impact if we spill 20% to west?
ben: rough calc: 20% spill to west1 with on-demand dedicated = +$35k/day. if we use burst capacity reserved pools maybe +$12k/day. we can throttle non-critical jobs first.
ops-bot: rollback job queued: microcode-rollback-us-east1-racks-10-14 (initiated)
maya: first drain completed on node07, pods moved, no new Xid in 4m. node still shows network retransmits but less frequent.
ravi: started isolation test on node07: disabled SR-IOV VF for NIC -> no Xid for 6m. looks like VF fragmentation triggers link storms under heavy host traffic.
lina: patch idea: disable SR-IOV on affected NICs until vendor patch; or pin GPU workloads to non-VF NICs.
sre-oncall: action items: 1) continue rollback for racks 10-14 (in progress) 2) canary drains 1 node per rack, wait 10m 3) temporarily disable SR-IOV on affected hosts 4) if rollback doesn't reduce errors in 20m, start controlled spill to west1 and throttle batch jobs.
alex: please add a short status post to #incidents when we hit rollback completion or spill start. keep me posted.
ben: posting cost/time tradeoff in pager: spill will be slow to start, give us breathing room.
maya: log note: after rollback in rack12, Xid dropped from ~60/min to ~2/min on the canary. proceeding with cautious drains.
ravi: will open vendor ticket with NIC vendor + nv support; include pcie AER traces and SR-IOV config.
lina: leaving a small checklist here: `1) rollback confirmed; 2) canary drains ok; 3) SR-IOV disabled; 4) vendor case opened; 5) monitor for 2h`
sre-oncall: updating incident doc now and tagging SE and network owners. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks all. if anything spikes again call me. :phone:
ops-bot: [event] incident_update: rollback_result=partial canary_ok=true current_capacity_loss=6%
maya: current load redistribution in progress, will post final numbers in 30m.
